prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the receding geometry of the retail interior and tracks a foreground person moving into the space directly in front of the camera wearer across the five frames. In Frame 1, a bright foreground hand and phone at the bottom-left (~0.3-0.5 m, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) sit in front of a mid-ground clothing display wall (~1.2-1.8 m) to the right and a dark mirror cavity on the left, while in Frame 2 a bright object enters at the bottom-left corner (~0.5 m) ahead of the slatted clothing rack on the left (~1.2-1.5 m) and the white wall and dark doorway receding to the right (~1.5-2.5 m). Across Frames 3 to 5, a person enters from the left at ~0.5-0.8 m and steps directly in front of the camera wearer at ~0.5-0.7 m (within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the background rack ~1 m behind them), facing the camera wearer with their downward-tilted head brightest in Frame 4 (~0.4-0.5 m) and their right hand holding a phone (viewer's left, ~0.3-0.4 m) and raised left hand (viewer's right, ~0.4-0.5 m) protruding closest to the camera in front of their chest in Frame 5, while their lower body remains out of view below the frame. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly isolates the approaching person and their outstretched hands and phone from the visually busy patterned garments and plaid shirt behind them, while also showing the continuous slant of the wall plane from left to right. However, the depth map is unreliable on the mirror in Frame 1 (rendering the reflection as a deep black void rather than a flat surface at ~1.2 m), flattens the hanging garments into the wall plane in Frames 2-3, and shifts the background wall in Frames 4-5 to near-black due to relative depth normalization when the person and hands move very close.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map provides 2D silhouettes and class labels for major regions across Frames 2-5, after leaving Frame 1 entirely blank. In Frame 2 it segments the angled central wall (~1.5-2.0 m from the camera wearer, positioned between the unsegmented left clothing rack and right doorway), and in Frames 3 and 4 it tracks a pink 'person' mask entering from the left (~0.5-0.8 m) to the center (~0.5-0.7 m, within arm's reach), standing directly in front of and progressively occluding the left side of the background wall mask (~1 m behind the person). By Frame 5, the 'person' mask occupies the center-left foreground (~0.3-0.7 m) as the person faces toward the camera wearer with their lower torso cropped out at the bottom edge, and two small overlapping masks labeled 'tie' appear on the chest where the green lanyard and handheld phone sit within both the person's and camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.3-0.6 m). This map makes the 2D occlusion boundary between the approaching person's silhouette and the background wall in Frames 3-4 immediately distinct against the cluttered retail background. However, it is highly unreliable: it detects nothing in Frame 1, misclassifies the flat white wall as a 'refrigerator' in Frames 2-4 before dropping it completely in Frame 5, mislabels the lanyard and phone region as 'tie' in Frame 5 while failing to segment the phone or hanging clothes as separate instances, and merges the person's head, torso, and raised arms into a single flat mask that hides 3D relative depth and facing direction.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D yellow body keypoints and magenta hand skeletons on a black background, remaining completely empty in Frames 1-4 and detecting a skeleton only in Frame 5. In Frame 5, the yellow upper-body torso trapezoid and facial keypoints place the person in the center-left foreground (~0.5-0.7 m from the camera wearer, within arm's reach), facing toward the camera wearer with their head angled downward (eyes and nose keypoints below ear level, looking toward their chest area) and their body below the hips out of view at the bottom of the frame. The yellow arm links show both elbows flared outward to the left and right of the torso and both wrists brought inward in front of the chest (~0.3-0.5 m from the camera wearer and ~0.15 m apart from each other), where the person's right wrist (viewer's left) holds the phone and their left hand (viewer's right) is raised beside it. Compared to the RGB image alone, the skeleton in Frame 5 explicitly localizes the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hip joints despite the visually busy plaid flannel pattern and dark sunglasses. However, the pose map is unreliable across the sequence because it completely fails to detect the person in Frames 1, 3, and 4 (even when their full upper body and head are clearly in view in Frame 4), misses the magenta finger skeleton on the person's right hand holding the phone in Frame 5, and produces distorted, stretched magenta lines on the motion-blurred left hand that pull erroneously toward the lower-right elbow.
